# Configure Boundary OIDC authentication with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)

Boundary delegates authentication to Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) using the [OIDC (OpenID Connect) auth method](/boundary/docs/domain-model/auth-methods#oidc-auth-method-attributes), a common single sign-on (SSO) integration. You can register Boundary as either a HashiCorp Boundary enterprise application or a generic web application, then create the matching OIDC auth method in Boundary.

## Prerequisites

- An Azure account with access to Microsoft Entra ID. HashiCorp recommends using a test account that is not tied to another SSO method.
- Administrator access to Boundary.

## Register a Boundary application in Entra ID

You can register Boundary in Microsoft Entra ID using either the HashiCorp Boundary enterprise application from the Entra ID gallery, or by registering a generic web application. Both methods let Entra ID authenticate Boundary users and redirect them back to Boundary after a successful login.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Enterprise application" group="enterprise">

1. In the [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com/), navigate to **Microsoft Entra ID**, Click **+Add**, and then select **Enterprise application**.
1. Search for `hashicorp boundary`, and select the **HashiCorp Boundary** gallery application.
1. Name the application and select **Create**.
1. From the application's **Overview** page, select **Single sign-on**, and then select **Go to application** on the **OIDC-based Sign-on** page.
1. Select **Authentication** from the sidebar.
1. Under **Redirect URIs**, add the following URL to the **Web** platform, replacing `BOUNDARY_ADDR` with the address of your Boundary controller:

   ```plaintext
   https://BOUNDARY_ADDR/v1/auth-methods/oidc:authenticate:callback
   ```

1. Under **Front-channel logout URL**, add your Boundary address:

   ```plaintext
   https://BOUNDARY_ADDR
   ```

1. Select **Save**.
1. Select **Certificates & secrets** from the sidebar, select **New client secret**, and provide a description. Select an expiration for the secret, or specify a custom lifetime. Entra ID limits client secret lifetimes to 24 months or less, and Microsoft recommends an expiration of less than 12 months. Select **Add**. Copy the secret's **Value**, not its **Secret ID**. Entra ID does not display the value again after you leave the page. This maps to the auth method's `client-secret` attribute.
1. Return to the application's **Overview** page and record the **Application (Client) ID** and the **Directory (Tenant) ID**.
1. Select **Endpoints**, and copy the **OpenID Connect metadata document** URL up to and including `/v2.0`, for example `https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT_ID/v2.0`. This maps to the auth method's `issuer` attribute.
1. (Optional) If you configure the application to require user assignment, only the users and groups you assign can log in to Boundary. To assign them, navigate to **Entra ID** > **Enterprise apps** > **All applications**, select the application, and then select **Users and groups** > **Add user/group**.

   Group-based assignment requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license, and Entra ID does not support nested group memberships for application assignment.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Web application" group="web-app">

1. In the [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com/), navigate to **Microsoft Entra ID**, click **+Add**, and then select **App registration**.
1. Select **New registration**.
1. Name the application and select **Single tenant**.
1. Under **Redirect URI**, select **Web** and enter the following URL, replacing `BOUNDARY_ADDR` with the address of your Boundary controller:

   ```plaintext
   https://BOUNDARY_ADDR/v1/auth-methods/oidc:authenticate:callback
   ```

1. Select **Register**.
1. Select **Certificates & secrets** from the sidebar, select **New client secret**, and provide a description. Select an expiration for the secret, or specify a custom lifetime. Entra ID limits client secret lifetimes to 24 months or less, and Microsoft recommends an expiration of less than 12 months. Select **Add**. Copy the secret's **Value**, not its **Secret ID**. Entra ID does not display the value again after you leave the page. This maps to the auth method's `client-secret` attribute.
1. Select **Authentication** from the sidebar. Under **Front-channel logout URL**, add your Boundary address:

   ```plaintext
   https://BOUNDARY_ADDR
   ```

1. Select **Save**.
1. Return to the application's **Overview** page and record the **Application (Client) ID** and the **Directory (Tenant) ID**.
1. Select **Endpoints**, and copy the **OpenID Connect metadata document** URL up to and including `/v2.0`, for example `https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT_ID/v2.0`. This maps to the auth method's `issuer` attribute.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

<Note>

Refer to the [Microsoft Entra ID OIDC documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-protocols) for the latest OIDC endpoint formats, since they can vary by tenant configuration.

</Note>

## Create an OIDC auth method for Entra ID

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Select the scope in which you want to create the auth method.
1. Select **Auth Methods**, then select **New**.
1. Select **OIDC**, and complete the following fields:
   - **Name**: (Optional) An optional name for identification purposes.
   - **Description**: (Optional) An optional description of the auth method.
   - **Issuer**: (Required) The **OpenID Connect metadata document** URL, up to and including `/v2.0`.
   - **Client ID**: (Required) The application's **Application (Client) ID**.
   - **Client Secret**: (Required) The application's client secret **Value**.
   - **API URL Prefix**: (Required) The address where your Boundary controller is reachable by Entra ID, for example `https://BOUNDARY_ADDR`.
1. Select **Save**.
1. Select **Edit Form**, scroll to **Signing Algorithms**, add `RS256`, and select **Add**.
1. Select **Save**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

```shell-session
$ boundary auth-methods create oidc \
  -scope-id $SCOPE_ID \
  -issuer "https://login.microsoftonline.com/$TENANT_ID/v2.0" \
  -client-id "$CLIENT_ID" \
  -client-secret "$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -signing-algorithm RS256 \
  -api-url-prefix "https://BOUNDARY_ADDR" \
  -name "azure"
```

The `scope-id` determines which scope contains the auth method. Set it to `global` or to an org scope ID. If you omit `scope-id`, Boundary uses the `BOUNDARY_SCOPE_ID` environment variable, or defaults to `global`.

The `issuer`, `client-id`, and `client-secret` values come from the Entra ID application settings. The `api-url-prefix` must match the address where your Boundary controller is reachable by Entra ID.

Refer to the [auth-methods create](/boundary/docs/commands/auth-methods/create) command documentation for additional fields that you can use when you create OIDC auth methods.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Apply the following Terraform configuration:

```hcl
resource "boundary_auth_method_oidc" "provider" {
  name               = "Azure"
  description        = "OIDC auth method for Microsoft Entra ID"
  scope_id           = "SCOPE_ID"
  issuer             = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT_ID/v2.0"
  client_id          = "CLIENT_ID"
  client_secret      = "CLIENT_SECRET"
  signing_algorithms = ["RS256"]
  api_url_prefix     = "https://BOUNDARY_ADDR"
}
```

Replace `scope_id`, `issuer`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, and `api_url_prefix` with the values for your scope and Entra ID application.

Refer to the [boundary_auth_method_oidc](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/boundary/latest/docs/resources/auth_method_oidc) resource documentation for additional fields that you can use when you create OIDC auth methods.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Troubleshooting

#### `oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider`

If the `issuer` attribute does not exactly match the **OpenID Connect metadata document** URL, including the `/v2.0` suffix and tenant ID, activating the auth method fails with an error similar to the following:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```plaintext
oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider, expected "https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT_ID/" got "https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT_ID/v2.0"
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Update the auth method's `issuer` attribute to match the **OpenID Connect metadata document** URL exactly, and try again.

#### `AADSTS50105`

If you configure the application to require user assignment, Entra ID refuses to authenticate anyone you have not assigned to it, and returns the following error:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```plaintext
AADSTS50105: EntitlementGrantsNotFound - The signed in user isn't assigned to a role for the signed in app.
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Assign the user, or a group the user belongs to, to the application. Refer to the Microsoft documentation for [managing user and group assignment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/assign-user-or-group-access-portal) and [requiring user assignment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/what-is-access-management#requiring-user-assignment-for-an-app).

@include 'authentication/troubleshoot-oidc-not-primary.mdx'
